title: Content model
description: The step before the first screen spec of a project: the objects the product is about, their attributes, relations and actions (ORCA), agreed before any screen is invented. Screens are then DERIVED — each object gets its collection and/or detail, actions land on screens — and scripts/check-screen-spec.mjs verifies the derivation: every action names a spec that exists, every core attribute appears on the object's screen, and a spec of the project that no object claims is counted out loud.

id.description: The app folder name (apps/<id>) — it is how specs are traced back to this model.

roles.description: Who acts on the objects. Every action's roles must come from this list — the CTA matrix's row headers.

objects.description: The nouns that pass the litmus test: multiple instances, attributes of their own, purpose to the user. A noun that fails it is an attribute or a vocabulary, not an object.

core.description: What makes an instance itself — the fields a screen about this object may not drop. Checked textually against the object's screen spec.

meta.description: Secondary facts. Not checked; recorded so the split core/meta is a decision, not an accident.

to.description: Another object declared in this model.

verb.description: One cell of the CTA matrix: role does verb to object.

screen.description: The spec id where this action lives. An action with no screen is a requirement nobody placed — allowed while open, counted out loud.

constraint.description: What limits the action, in one sentence (e.g. an Area Admin only within their own area).

provenBy.description: The behaviour that proves this action: <spec-id>#<behaviour-id>. Closes the chain requirement -> action -> behaviour -> test; the check fails when the behaviour does not exist.

screens.description: Where this object lives: its collection and/or its detail. Both optional — but an object with neither is a model entry no screen carries, and the check says so.

vocabularies.description: Nouns that FAILED the litmus test, recorded with the reason — so the next session does not re-litigate why area is a field and not a screen.
